concepts.why: The patient presents with right iliac fossa pain, nausea, and diarrhea, and the abdominal CT scan demonstrates a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole with a pericecal collection, which is consistent with appendicitis.
The patient has a history of laparoscopic appendectomy and presents with a pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips, which suggests a postoperative abscess.
The patient presents with right lower quadrant pain and elevated C-reactive protein level, which could be consistent with diverticulitis.
The patient is febrile and has an elevated white-blood-cell count with neutrophilia, which suggests an intra-abdominal infection.
The abdominal CT scan demonstrates a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole, which could be consistent with cecal inflammation.

rationales.F01: Right iliac fossa pain is a common symptom of appendicitis.
rationales.F04: Pain in the right lower quadrant is consistent with appendicitis or cecal inflammation.
rationales.F08: A swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole is highly suggestive of appendicitis.
rationales.F09: A pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips is more likely to be a postoperative abscess.
rationales.F10: A history of laparoscopic appendectomy increases the likelihood of a postoperative abscess.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a 25-mm pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips and a history of laparoscopic appendectomy 8 months earlier strongly supports the diagnosis of a postoperative abscess, despite the patient having had an appendectomy, the current findings are more indicative of a complication from the previous surgery.
